newsitem.title: USA: AmEx stock rise attributed to merger talk.
newsitem.headline: AmEx stock rise attributed to merger talk.

text.p: An intraday rise in shares of American Express Co to a new 52-week high of 63-7/8 Thursday was attributed to renewed takeover rumors, said Salomon Brothers analyst Tom Facciola.

"We keep hearing the Citibank rumors over and over again," the analyst said. In early January, there were published reports that Citibank parent Citicorp had held abortive merger talks with American Express.
A spokeswoman for American Express Thursday declined comment, citing a policy of not responding to rumors or speculation.
At the time the rumors first surfaced, American Express said it was not then talking to anyone.
Facciola also said of a Citicorp-American Express combinaton, "I don't think it's happening. The legal hurdles would be tremendous."
The analyst noted that non-bank financial stocks have been "on fire" recently after lagging for a while.
Many non-bank financial stocks rose this week after Banc One Corp announced an agreement to acquire First USA Inc in a $7.3 billion stock deal.
At a meeting with analysts Tuesday after the release of its fourth-quarter earnings, Citicorp chairman John Reed declined to comment on American Express rumors.
But Reed discussed acquisition strategy in general, and said any acquisition undertaken by Citicorp would have to support the company's business direction.
American Express stock closed off 3/4 at 60-3/4. The intraday rise evaporated as the overall U.S. stock market fell sharply in late trading.

American Express is expected to report fourth-quarter earnings next week. The consensus view tracked by Institutional Brokers Estimate System is $0.43 per share for the quarter, with a range of $0.41 to $0.45.
